comments.body: @copilot-swe-agent please enable the option "Allow edits and access to secrets by maintainers" on your PR. For more information, [see the documentation](https://docs.github.com/en/pull-requests/collaborating-with-pull-requests/working-with-forks/allowing-changes-to-a-pull-request-branch-created-from-a-fork).

> Checkstyle 14.1.0’s built-in `UnnecessaryFullyQualifiedType` does not inspect class literals.

Just to make sure I understand: is this merely a statement of fact or is it an observation of a change? That is, for example, has it never been the case that the built-in `UnnecessaryFullyQualifiedType` checked this or is this a new true statement about the world (i.e. "... but in 13.x-or-some-version it **did** do this type of checking")?

edit: I bring this up partially because we happen to be on [Checkstyle 13.11.0](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/blob/2e2020419b4be86524ef3e436ec2347089cfd1f0/gradle/build.versions.toml#L17) right now, not 14.1.0.

It has never done this checking. `UnnecessaryFullyQualifiedType` is a new built-in check in Checkstyle 14.1.0, so it does not exist in our current 13.11.0 version; I evaluated upgrading to use it. Testing 14.1.0 showed that the new check does not cover class literals, including the motivating `TopNExec.class` case. It also surfaced 1,108 existing violations in other type contexts. This PR therefore keeps Checkstyle at 13.11.0 and adds the narrowly scoped class-literal check. I’ll clarify the PR description—the current wording is misleading.
Going to close this in favor of bumping spotless when it is bug-free
